english: And by my boon you shall become as dear as life itself to her.
And Radhika will know of the secret love between you two.
O fortunate one, you shall become equal to Radha in Govinda's regard.
Having spoken thus, and having given the Goddess that sixteen-syllabled mantra.

sanskrit: मन्त्रं तस्यै जगद्धाता स्तोत्रं च कवचं परम् ।
english: The creator of the world gave her the mantra, the hymn of praise, and the supreme protective armor.
And the entire method of worship, and the sequential procedure of preliminary ritual practice.
Having given a great blessing, he then vanished.
And she, through Brahma's teaching, in the sacred hermitage of Badarika.
She repeated the supreme mantra that had been desired from a former birth.

sanskrit: दिव्यं द्वादशवर्षं च पूजां चैव चकार सा ।
english: And for twelve divine years she performed worship.

sanskrit: सिद्धे तपसि मन्त्रे च वरं प्राप्य यथेप्सितम् ।
english: When the austerity and the mantra had borne fruit, having obtained the boon as desired.
And she enjoyed the great fortune that is very rare in all the worlds.

sanskrit: सिद्धे फले नराणां च दुःखं तत् सुखमुत्तमम् ।
english: When the fruit is attained, that suffering of men becomes the highest happiness.

sanskrit: भुक्त्वा पीत्वा च संतुष्टा शयनं च चकार सा ।
english: Having eaten and drunk and being satisfied, she then went to bed.
On the delightful bed there, anointed with flowers and sandalwood paste.
The fifteenth chapter, named 'The Granting of the Boon of Tulsi.'
Salutation to the sage of Brahma, [placed] on the head.
note: Likely a ritual nyasa formula assigning a mantra to a body part; terse fragment.

english: Salutation to you of many hands, and salutation indeed to the many-headed one.
Salutation to you of many eyes, and salutation indeed to the one of manifold glory.
Salutation to you of many throats, and salutation to you the boundless one.
May there be salutation to the one of endless power, salutation to you the greatly fearsome one.
Salutation to the fierce one, the peaceful one, who grants peace to devotees.
Salutation to the teacher of all worlds, who is the very form of the syllable Om.

sanskrit: नमः स्वर्णाकर्षणाय, स्वर्णाभाय च ते नमः ।
english: Salutation to the one who draws forth gold, and salutation to you of golden radiance.
To the one who is a refuge in time of fear for devotees, who grants all desires.
O glorious Bhairava, lord of wealth, I take refuge in and adore you.
This is the hymn of the great glorious Bhairava, a hymn very rare to obtain.
Consisting of mantra, greatly meritorious, bestowing all prosperity.
Whoever recites it daily with single-pointed concentration is freed from sins.
He surely obtains the wish-fulfilling gem, the wish-granting cow, and the wish-fulfilling tree.
That man obtains a heap of gold, indeed attainment itself.
In his dream, the glorious Bhairava, teacher of the world, appears in person.
He indeed gives a heap of gold at that very moment — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: सर्वदा यः पठेत् स्तोत्रं, भैरवस्य महात्मनः ।।
english: Whoever always recites the hymn of the great-souled Bhairava.
note: Sentence continues into the next verse-line.

sanskrit: लोक-त्रयं वशी कुर्यात्, अचलां श्रियं चाप्नुयात् ।
english: He can bring the three worlds under his control, and obtains unshakeable prosperity.
His enemies certainly perish, and [the one who neglects this hymn] would suffer the loss of fortune.
note: Two half-lines read as joined; likely elliptical verse, exact syntax uncertain.

english: The best of men obtains imperishable happiness forever.
The king of mantras, endowed with fifty-eight syllables, has been proclaimed.
It pacifies the suffering of poverty and brings about the attraction of gold.
Krishna gives divine sight to Arjuna.
Saketa gives a sweet to Abhaya with his hand.
The delighted man travels by car from Jaipur to Jodhpur.
Shyamkishor has books.
Rama, the jewel among kings, is ever victorious.
I worship Rama, the lord of Rama (Lakshmi's lord).
There is no higher refuge than Rama.
I am a servant of Rama.
May my mind ever be absorbed in Rama.

sanskrit: मयूरः सर्वेषु पक्षिषु सुन्दरतमः अस्ति । तस्य मनोहरः बर्हः भवति । अतः एव अस्य बर्ही इति नाम । मयूरीणां तु बर्हः नास्ति ।
english: The peacock is the most beautiful of all birds. It has a captivating tail-crest. For this very reason its name is 'barhī' (the one with a tail-crest). Peahens, however, do not have this tail-crest.

sanskrit: यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ।
english: Tell me decisively what is truly best for me; I am your disciple — instruct me, who have taken refuge in you.
note: Echoes the well-known Bhagavad Gita 2.7 line.

sanskrit: ते तु भगगुदबस्ति प्रदेशदारणाश्च भगंदरा इत्युच्यन्ते ।
english: Those fissures in the region of the anus and bladder are called 'bhagandara' (anal fistula).
note: Ayurvedic medical terminology.

sanskrit: बीजमत्रांः ॐ का्रं क्रीं कौं सः भोमाय नमः।
english: The seed-syllables here: Om, krāṃ, krīṃ, kauṃ, saḥ — salutation to Bhauma (the planet Mars).
note: Bīja mantra syllables are ritual sounds without ordinary lexical meaning; likely OCR-corrupted.

sanskrit: -- युक्ताहारविहारस्य आह्रियते इति आहारः अन्नम्, विहरणं विहारः पादक्रमः,
english: ...of one whose diet and conduct are disciplined — 'āhāra' (food) is so called because it is taken in, [and] 'vihāra' (conduct) is the manner of proceeding,
note: Mid-sentence fragment of a grammatical/etymological commentary; continues into the next entry.

sanskrit: युक्तौ नियतपरिमाणौ यस्य सः युक्ताहारविहारः तस्य, तथा युक्तचेष्टस्य युक्ता
english: ...he whose food and conduct are both fixed in measure is called 'yuktāhāravihāra'; likewise, of one whose effort is regulated...
note: Continuing fragment, sentence is cut off mid-clause in the source.

english: To the one fit to be served like Kumara himself, and to the one who is beheld by the thunderbolt-eyed one.
note: Elliptical epithet from a longer namaskara-stotra; verb 'namah' implied from context, not present in this line.

english: To Rama, to the lotus-naveled one, and ever to the one praised by Vayu.
Constant salutation to the one whose story concerns king Uparichara Vasu, to Krishna.
And to the one dwelling in Shvetadvipa, whose pair of feet the liberated ones worship.
To you, Damodara, always, and to the one who resembles a dark-blue cloud.
To Narayana, lord of the sacred hill, and to the one for whom Brahma ordained a festival.
note: Likely refers to a specific hill-shrine name; exact referent uncertain.

english: And to the giver of the boons sought by petitioners, who removes affliction from every direction.
To the one who dwells on Simhachalam, and to the glorious Narayana.
And salutation, salutation to the one who takes the life of the evil-minded, to Vamana.
Salutation to you, Rama the ender of the warrior-kings, and to the one in fish-form.
note: Refers to Parashurama and the Matsya avatar.

english: And salutation, salutation to the remover of the Pandavas' afflictions, to Shridhara.
To the one dear in form, dear as the boar, and to the best of white boars.
note: Refers to Varaha, the boar incarnation; phrasing partly obscure.

english: And to the one dear through being the Vedanta-teacher known as the Brahmin Krishna.
Salutation ever to Achyuta, and to the one whose abode is the Blue Mountain.
note: Niladri likely refers to Jagannath Puri.

sanskrit: गोविन्दाय नमो नित्यं श्रीनिवासाय ते नमः ॥
english: Salutation ever to Govinda, salutation to you, Shrinivasa.

sanskrit: अथ देवस्य वाम भागे दीप स्थापनं करिष्ये।
english: Now I shall place the lamp on the left side of the deity.
note: Ritual instruction.

sanskrit: ॐ हरये नमः । ॐ श्रीकृष्णाय नमः ।
english: Om, salutation to Hari. Om, salutation to Sri Krishna.

sanskrit: हीं बीजं सदापातु नभो, गुहो च पादयो॥
english: May the seed-syllable 'hrīṃ' ever protect the head, and Guha protect the feet.
note: Ritual nyasa formula assigning protective syllables to body parts; brief/possibly corrupted.

sanskrit: कदाचित् कुप्यते माता न उदरस्था हरितकी।।
english: Sometimes the mother becomes angry, but the harītakī within the womb does not.
note: Reads as proverbial or riddle-like; literal sense uncertain.

english: [Her] who delights in ever dwelling on his chest, who increases his forbearance.
note: Fragment describing a goddess (likely Lakshmi) on Vishnu's chest.

english: I take refuge in the two feet of Sri Venkatesha.
I take refuge in the two feet of Sri Venkatesha.
[Those two feet,] praised as being at the supreme abode of Vishnu.
note: Sentence continues into the next line.

sanskrit: यौ मध्व उत्स इति भोग्य तयाप्युपात्तौ ।
english: ...which two feet, described as a fount of honey, were taken up by her too as an object of delight.
note: Continuation of the previous fragment.

english: On the peak of Venkata hill, at the very crown of the Vedas.
[Those two feet,] regarded as the ornament of the peak of Venkata hill.
note: Continuing fragment.

sanskrit: स्यां किङ्करो वृषगिरीश न जातु मह्यम् ।
english: O Lord of Vrishagiri, may I become your servant; may there never be [pride] in me.

sanskrit: जगन्नाथः स्वामी नयन पथ गामी भवतु मे ॥
english: May Lord Jagannath, the Master, ever walk the path of my sight.
note: Well-known line from the Jagannathashtakam attributed to Adi Shankaracharya.

sanskrit: अयम् धातुः इदित् अस्ति, अतः इदितो नुम् धातोःइत्यनेन धातौ नुमागमः भवति, येन "मुन्ख्" इति स्वरूपं जायते। अग्रे परसवर्णेन नकारस्य ङकारादेशः विधीयते, येन अन्तिमरूपेषु सर्वत्र ङकारः एव दृश्यते, न हि नकारः । अतः अत्र अन्वेषणसौलभ्यार्थम् मूलरूपे अपि ङकारः एव निर्दिष्टः अस्ति ।
english: This root carries the indicatory marker 'i', so by the rule 'iditaḥ num dhātoḥ' an augment 'num' is inserted into the root, producing the form 'muṅkh'. Subsequently, by assimilation to the following sound, 'na' is replaced with 'ṅa', so in the final forms only 'ṅa' appears, never 'na'. Therefore, for ease of lookup, 'ṅa' is shown even in the base form here.
note: Technical Paninian grammatical commentary.

sanskrit: व्रणे कीट इवास्वाद्य वयः कार्यं न भस्मसात् ॥
english: Like a worm tasting a wound, [yet] time does not reduce one's duty to ashes.
note: Obscure gnomic verse fragment; reading uncertain.

sanskrit: ओम् ज्ञानिनामपि चेतांसि देवी भगवती हि सा।
english: Om. She indeed is the divine Goddess who [draws] even the minds of the wise.
note: Echoes Devi Mahatmya 1.42.

english: Remembering [you], sleepless, I passed the night.
Note: 'vinidra' means 'one from whom sleep has departed', i.e. sleepless.
note: Grammatical gloss explaining the previous word.

sanskrit: देवाः दे दबू, नेसं ११२७, नेवाः समाज, येँ दे दबू ।
english: [Not translated — this line is Newari-language proper nouns/institution names in Devanagari script ("Deva Dey Dabu", Nepal Sambat year 1127, "Newa: Samaj"), not Sanskrit prose.]
note: Flagged rather than force-translated as Sanskrit; appears to be Newari.

sanskrit: ॐ नमो भगवते वासुदेवायकृष्णं वन्दे जगद्गुरुम्
english: Om, salutation to the Lord Vasudeva. I bow to Krishna, the teacher of the world.
Thus, in the glorious Mahabharata, in the collection of one hundred thousand [verses]...
note: Standard colophon formula; sentence is cut off (incomplete in source).

english: Om, salutation to Sri Ganesha.
Om Hrim, salutation to Subrahmanya. To the power of knowledge.
To the one who is a mass of pure consciousness. To the one whose eternal abode is amid the island shaped of the sky of consciousness.
note: Dense philosophical epithet-stotra; figurative language.

english: To the crest-jewel amid the great ocean of the bliss of consciousness.
To the one shining as the sky of consciousness, situated in the great twelve-spoked lotus.
note: Refers to a specific yogic/tantric visualization (dvadashara chakra).

english: To the one skilled in the great piercing of the three [psychic] knots. To the true Guru.
To the lord of the stainless sky situated amid the heart-lotus. To the one whose abode is the peaceful mountain.
To the one characterized by unbroken knowledge. To the one free of distinctions of same-kind, different-kind, or internal difference.
note: Vedantic philosophical terminology (sajātīya/vijātīya/svagata bheda).

english: To Shiva the Guru. To the one whose abode of consciousness, arising at the mouth of the root chakra, is the crown aperture.
note: Yogic/tantric physiological terminology.

english: Om, salutation to the one whose own form is self-luminous light, seated blissfully in his own sovereign realm.
To the one known through the great inward silence. To the one of pure conscious essence.
To the great treasure of the play of consciousness that is non-dual supreme bliss. To the illuminator of the three spheres.
Om, salutation to the one who is the Self of all. To the one whose own nature is the intended meaning of the great sayings beginning with 'Tat Tvam Asi'.
To the one who dwells at the boundary of the path of the [chakric] supports. To the ocean of waveless bliss.
To the one whose own form is the auspicious light of the lamp of consciousness. To the sovereign lord of the city of the six chakras.
To the single eye of all the worlds. To the one free of manifest phenomena. To the one without support.
Om, salutation to the one situated in the great Anahata chakra. To the witness of the three states [waking, dream, deep sleep].
To the one pervading everything from Brahma down to the smallest worm. To the refuge of all the worlds' gods.
To the great, supra-mundane, divine Person. To the sun that dispels the darkness of ignorance.
To the one who bestows the bliss of imperishable knowledge. To the one adorned with inconceivable divine glory.
Om, salutation to the orb of consciousness situated in the eternally full space of consciousness.

sanskrit: भक्तिप्रदानाय कृपावतीर्णं तं सोमनाथं शरणं प्रपद्ये ।
english: I take refuge in that Somanatha, who descended out of compassion to bestow devotion.
note: From the Dvadasha Jyotirlinga Stotra.

english: I bow to that unique Mallikarjuna, the bridge across the ocean of worldly existence.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Mallikarjuna.

english: For protection from untimely death, I salute Mahakala, the great lord.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Mahakaleshwar.

english: I praise the one Shiva, Lord Omkareshwar, who ever dwells in the city of Mandhata.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Omkareshwar.

english: I bow to that glorious Vaidyanatha, whose lotus feet are worshipped by gods and demons alike.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Vaidyanath.

sanskrit: महाद्रिपार्श्वे च तटे रमन्तं सम्पूज्यमानं सततं मुनीन्द्रैः ।
english: [Him] who delights on the mountainside and shore, ever worshipped by the great sages.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra, likely describing Bhimashankar.

english: I praise the one Shiva, Lord Kedareshwar, worshipped by gods, demons, yakshas, and great serpent-beings.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Kedarnath.

sanskrit: श्रीरामचन्द्रेण समर्पितं तं रामेश्वराख्यं नियतं नमामि ।
english: I constantly bow to that linga named Rameshwara, consecrated by Sri Ramachandra.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Rameshwaram.

sanskrit: सदैव भीमादिपदप्रसिद्दं तं शङ्करं भक्तहितं नमामि ।
english: I bow to that Shankara, ever famed by the name Bhima, who is ever beneficial to devotees.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Bhimashankar.

english: I take refuge in the glorious Vishwanatha, lord of Varanasi, protector of those without protector.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Vishwanath.

english: I salute and take refuge in the one named Ghrishneshwar, whose nature is exceedingly generous.
note: Jyotirlinga Stotra — Grishneshwar.

sanskrit: छन्दसि इत्येव। वसन्तशब्दाच् छन्दसि विषये ठञ् प्रत्ययो भवति शैषिकः। ऋत्वणो ऽपवादः। मधुश्च माधवश्च वासन्तिकावृतू।
english: Only in Vedic usage. From the word 'vasanta', in the Vedic sense, the general suffix 'ṭhañ' occurs — an exception to the rule 'ṛtvaṇ'. Thus 'madhu' and 'mādhava' are the two seasons of spring.
note: Technical Paninian grammatical commentary.

sanskrit: आ नो भद्रो  क्रत्वो यन्तु विश्वतः
english: Let noble thoughts come to us from every side.
note: Famous Rigvedic verse, RV 1.89.1.

english: Among all duties, the eternal dharma alone is the most excellent.
All [other] duties arise and pass, but the eternal one alone is everlasting.
Then, in mind, he was intent upon that thought.
Contemplated by him together was the matter of the suitability of the two young men,
note: Continues into the next line.

english: What sort of relationship will there be between the father and the two sons?
It will go entirely in vain — there is no doubt about this.
Then, for the sake of the lineage of heroes.
Or indeed, who will say for certain,
note: Continues into the next line.

english: ...that the ornament of Rama's lineage would not desire [it]?
note: Continuation of the previous fragment; exact syntax uncertain.

english: Then, if it were not to happen,
note: Sentence fragment, continues beyond the corpus excerpt.
